evidence_against.relevance: Alex initiated two one-on-one outings with Jordan, which could indicate special interest, though one concerned a group-shared interest.
Remembering Jordan's presentation, sending encouragement, and bringing drink options show personal attentiveness.
Extended post-event texting that included personal updates could reflect interest beyond routine group interaction.

evidence_supporting.relevance: Alex shows similar attentiveness, gift-giving, and one-on-one social behavior toward several other people, supporting general friendliness.
Across ten weeks, Alex gave no explicit romantic label, statement, or physical signal.
Alex postponed Jordan's proposed dinner twice and did not offer a replacement date during the next two weeks.

recommended_action.explanation: The record better supports general friendliness than special or romantic interest, so maintaining the current level of engagement is proportionate.

uncertainty_explanation: The one-on-one plans, attentiveness, and extended texting leave some possibility of special interest, but Alex's similar behavior toward others, lack of explicit romantic signals, and failure to reschedule the proposed dinner make general friendliness the better-supported interpretation.
